_comment: Curated A16 test-point data, hand-authored from the service manuals rather than
parsed. Like A14, this board generates no supply Chapter 2 tabulates -- there is no
Table 2-x of A16 rails -- so every published expectation comes from the §5-22
procedure, from the 35xx fault codes in §5-2, or from the theory in §2-139 … §2-154.
Seventeen test points, and §5-22 names ten of them. TP10 (PA COM) is the reference
for every measurement on this assembly unless a step says otherwise -- §5-22 step 1
says so outright, and fault code 3508 repeats it as COM=TP10, HI=TP6.
Signal names and their sheet/zone references are transcribed from the legend box in
the top right corner of schematic sheet 1, which prints them as 'TP1 = PA SENSE DC
(PG2D7)' -- page 2, zone D7. The same legend gives each point's physical type by
symbol: a wire loop, a pad, or the high voltage marker. That matches Table 6-20,
which lists TP1-5, TP7-13, TP16 and TP17 as one line of 14 'JUMPER,WIRE,NONINSUL,
0.200CTR' (stock 816090) and TP6, TP14 and TP15 as three separate single sockets
with three different stock numbers (170480, 149138, 149120). So fourteen take a clip
lead and three take a pin.
Two kinds of expectation needed care:
* Several of the published checks are *relative* -- TP6 is '10 times TP3 ±5%',
TP7 is 'the same as TP6 ±10 mV', TP8 is 'TP7 divided by 100 ±1%', U9 pin 6 is
'TP12 divided by 8 ±1%'. Those carry an absolute nominal here so the app has
something to show, marked inferred, with the published rule spelled out in the
note. The rule is the acceptance test; the absolute number is a convenience.
* Where the manual publishes no band at all it is left with no band. TP12 is the
clearest case: step 12 says to measure the 13 V reference at DAC TP2 and verify
TP12 'is the same', without a tolerance. Writing ±1% there would invent an
acceptance test the manual declines to give.
Step numbers cite §5-22's own printed numbering, which is a single sequence of 12 --
unlike A14, this board's troubleshooting is printed as one section.

testpoints.note: Output of the sense-current cancellation circuit, and the signal routed to the Switch Matrix (A8) for the OUT/SENSE HI or SENSE HI binding posts. No level is published for TP1 on its own: §5-22 step 11 uses it as the reference for the one measurement that matters here, the 2 V ±25 mV between U1 pin 6 and TP1 at 100 V dc. Sense-current cancellation is active only in the dc 220 V range, so at any ac setting this node is doing nothing.

The dc input node of the amplifier, ahead of the 25 kΩ leg of the HR8 resistor network. The manual publishes no bench value here, but fault 3511 tabulates exactly this node's voltage for four DAC settings and reads it through MUX5 rather than at the test point. Those are the states below. They are simply the output divided by the dc gain of -20, so any other dc output gives its own expected input the same way. Marked inferred because the numbers are published as a diagnostic limit, not as a §5-22 step.

OSC OUT HI as it arrives at the 4.99 kΩ input resistor R17 through relay K10A. This is the first measurement of the procedure and the one that separates 'the amplifier is misbehaving' from 'the amplifier is being fed the wrong thing'. With the calibrator at 22 V and a gain of -10, 2.2 V here is what produces 22 V out. If it is wrong, nothing downstream is worth measuring -- check K10 and its drive circuit first.

Input stage output. The published check is a polarity test, not a level: measure pin 10 of the HR8 hybrid, note whether it is positive or negative, then verify TP4 is properly inverting with respect to it. Not inverting means the input stage is probably at fault; inverting correctly means the fault is more likely in the mid stage. No number is given for either node, so none is recorded.

The reference the input stage's non-inverting side is tied to, which changes with function: SW3 inverted by U8 turns on Q51 to reference it to R COM in the dc 220 V range, or Q50 to reference it to OS COM in ac. So a static reading here means nothing without knowing which function is selected -- what it is good for is confirming that SW3 and the Q50/Q51 pair are doing what the function calls for. The manual tabulates no value.

The Power Amplifier output, and the assembly's most important single node. It is a dedicated socket rather than a wire loop and the sheet 1 legend marks it with the high voltage symbol: in normal operation it reaches 220 V rms with the ±PA rails at up to ±365 V a few components away. Fault code 3508 names it explicitly as the HI point, with TP10 as COM, for the manual measurement that decides between A16 and A14. R120 and L10 isolate it from capacitive loads.

states.label: 22 V at 1 kHz, operate
states.setup: Set the calibrator to 22 V at 1 kHz, operate. Measure ac.
states.note: The published check is '10 times the voltage measured at TP3, ±5%'. With TP3 at its own 2.2 V ±5% that is 22 V, which is the number shown; the acceptance test is the ratio to whatever TP3 actually reads. Correct here means skip to step 8; incorrect means go on to step 3.

states.label: 22 V at 1 kHz, operate — dc offset
states.note: Published as 'less than 10 mV'. A large dc offset riding on a correct ac amplitude points at the output stage bias chain rather than at the signal path.

states.label: 0 V dc standby, mid stage at +0.8 V
states.setup: 0 V dc, standby, with an external 100 Ω 1/4 W carbon-film resistor from TP10 to 1ST MID STAGE OUT (left side of R41). Which of the two states applies is decided by reading the mid stage output first.

states.label: 0 V dc standby, mid stage at -1.1 V
states.setup: Same as above. The mid stage output sits at one of two levels and TP6 is checked against whichever one it is.

testpoints.condition: 22 V at 1 kHz, operate, with the two monitoring-defeat jumpers re-installed.
testpoints.note: PA SENSE AC arriving at the 220 V range ac attenuator input, pin 1 of network Z1, through relay K16. The published check is not this number: it is that TP7 and TP6 read the same within ±10 mV. TP7 is tied to TP6 out at the load rather than on the board, so the two being equal is a check on the whole sense path. If they differ, check relay K16B and its drive circuit; and if K16B is sound, the manual's own note says PA OUT HI may be open from PA SENSE AC elsewhere in the calibrator, which is not an A16 fault at all.

The 220 V range ac attenuator output, one hundredth of its input. The published check is 'the voltage measured at TP7 divided by 100, ±1%', so the 0.22 V shown is what that comes to when TP7 is at 22 V. Step 9 also asks for an oscilloscope here to look for distortion, which no meter reading will show. A bad ratio or visible distortion points at Z1, U4, Q58 and Q54. Note that the ±1% band is tight enough to be sensitive to which value of Z1's input leg is correct -- see the caveat about 396 kΩ and 400 kΩ.

The low end of the 175 kΩ/25 kΩ internal calibration network on HR8, switched between R COM, ACOM, DAC OUT HI and BSRF13 by relays K1 and K3 and switches U5A/U5C/U5D depending on which step of the internal calibration is running. Nothing is published for it, and a static reading is meaningless because what it is connected to depends on what the software is doing. Fault codes 3527 and 3528 are the tests that exercise it.

testpoints.source: §5-22 step 1; §5-2 fault code 3508; Figure 7-19 sheet 1 legend (PG3D8)
testpoints.note: Power amplifier common, and the reference for every measurement on this assembly unless a step says otherwise -- §5-22 step 1 says exactly that, and fault code 3508 names it as COM for the DMM check that decides between A16 and A14. It is also the far end of the external 100 Ω resistor that steps 4, 6 and 7 call for. It arrives at P701 pins 24A/24C and is clamped to LH COM by CR65 and CR66.

Sense common, in on P702 pins 32A/32C with the ±17 S supplies either side of it, and clamped to LH COM by CR63 and CR64. Step 12 uses it as a jumper target rather than as a measurement: U5 pin 1 is jumpered to TP11 to set up the 220 V dc internal calibration network check. That jumper is one of the three §5-22 leaves behind, so sweep for it afterwards.

testpoints.condition: 0 V dc, standby, with U5 pin 1 jumpered to SCOM (TP11).
testpoints.note: The buffered 13 V reference at the top of the internal calibration network. The published check is a comparison, not a band: measure the 13 V reference at TP2 of the DAC assembly (common to DAC TP3), note the reading, then verify TP12 is the same. No tolerance is given, so none is recorded here. A mismatch points at U5, K3 and their drive circuit. TP12 is then the reference for the one number step 12 does publish -- U9 pin 6 must equal TP12 divided by 8, ±1%.

The internal calibration return line back to the adc on the DAC assembly (A11), reached through relays K4, K10B and K11 depending on which network is being calibrated. Every one of fault codes 3527, 3528 and 3529 is measured through this line, so a fault here makes all three fire together while the amplifier itself is fine. Like TP9, it carries whatever the software has selected, so no static value exists to publish.

testpoints.condition: 0 V dc, standby, with an external 100 Ω 1/4 W carbon-film resistor from TP10 to 1ST MID STAGE OUT (the left side of R41).
testpoints.note: Output stage bias current, read as the voltage across the TP14-TP15 pair rather than to PA COM -- this is the one measurement on the board that is not referenced to TP10. The voltage across R74 and R35 sets the bias, and equals the voltage across Q7 (a Vbe multiplier, 1 + (R23+R26)/R32) minus four Vbe drops for Q4, Q5, Q10 and Q11. The output bias current it corresponds to is 50 mA per §2-145. The manual does not state a polarity for the measurement, only a magnitude.

The other half of the bias adjust pair. The published expectation belongs to the pair, not to either pad on its own, and is recorded on TP14: 0.92 V ±20% measured between TP14 and TP15. Both pads are sockets rather than wire loops, with different stock numbers from each other and from TP6.

Reference common. Q51, turned on by SW3 through inverter U8, ties the input stage reference to R COM in the dc 220 V range, and §2-154 notes ACOM is connected to RCOM through Q51 during the internal cal offset step. Not used by any §5-22 measurement, but it is the common the dc reference chain is built on.

Oscillator reference common, the return the 220 V range ac attenuator works against: control line C0*, inverted by U8, turns on Q58 to connect U4's non-inverting input to OSC RCOM. So it is the common that matters for the TP7 and TP8 measurements even though §5-22 references those to TP10 like everything else.

probePoints.label: 1ST MID STAGE OUT (left side of R41)
probePoints.condition: 0 V dc, standby, with an external 100 Ω 1/4 W carbon-film resistor connected from TP10 to this node.
probePoints.note: The mid stage output, and the node the whole bias-current investigation turns on. It sits at one of two stable levels and the manual accepts either; which one it is decides what TP6 should read in step 7. R41 is a 1 W 200 kΩ carbon composition resistor biasing Q12, so 'the left side of R41' is the drain node, not the supply end. The external 100 Ω resistor is a load the step calls for, not a normal part of the circuit -- fit it before measuring and remove it afterwards.

states.label: With Q12 removed
states.setup: Only if neither state above is met: remove Q12 from the assembly and measure again.
states.note: Still wrong with Q12 out means the 8 mA current source is at fault -- CR53, Q31, Q32 and R87. Correct with Q12 out means the input stage or mid stage is. Q12 is one of the two 800 V mid stage MOSFETs and is ESD sensitive; handle and reseat it carefully.

probePoints.label: HR8 pin 10 (hybrid op amp output)
probePoints.note: Read for polarity only. Note whether this is positive or negative, then check that TP4 -- the input stage output -- is properly inverting with respect to it. HR8 is the heated-substrate hybrid carrying the input stage op amp and both resistor networks; its inputs are protected by CR13 and CR14 and its oven is regulated by the Q38/Q35 heater circuit on sheet 3. If the oven is not regulating, fault 3520 fires and this reading should not be trusted.

probePoints.label: U1 pin 7 (SC+ supply)
probePoints.note: The positive supply for the sense-current cancellation op amp, bootstrapped off the output stage by zener VR15 (18 V) so that it floats with PA OUT HI instead of sitting on a fixed rail. That is why it is measured against PA COM at 0 V output and why it cannot be checked meaningfully with the amplifier driving.

probePoints.label: U1 pin 4 (SC- supply)
probePoints.conflict: Step 10 is headed 'Check the SC+ and SC- supplies' but then calls this one 'the DC- supply'. There is no DC- signal on the assembly; the schematic and §2-145 both name this node SC-, generated by VR18 in the same way VR15 generates SC+. Read it as SC-.
probePoints.note: The negative supply for U1, bootstrapped off the -PA side of the output stage by zener VR18 (15 V). Note that SC+ and SC- are deliberately different magnitudes, 18 V and 15 V, so a pair of readings that are equal and opposite is itself suspicious.

probePoints.label: U1 pin 6 to TP1 (sense current cancellation output)
probePoints.condition: 100 V dc, operate. Measured between U1 pin 6 and TP1, not to PA COM.
probePoints.note: The tightest tolerance in the whole procedure -- ±25 mV on 2 V -- because this circuit exists to cancel a small error current precisely. U1 drives a current through R8 equal and opposite to the current in the 500 kΩ feedback resistor on HR8, so that the finite resistance of the connection to the load does not show up as an output error. It is active only in the dc 220 V range, which is why the step calls for 100 V dc rather than any ac setting.

probePoints.label: K11 pin 8 (attenuator output to RCL)
probePoints.note: The last stop on the attenuator output before it leaves the board on the RCL line. The published check is that it is the same as TP8; the 0.22 V shown is what that comes to with the calibrator at 22 V. TP8 correct and this wrong isolates the fault to relays K10B and K11 and their drive circuit rather than to the attenuator itself.

probePoints.label: U9 pin 6 (internal cal network output)
probePoints.condition: 0 V dc, standby, with U5 pin 1 jumpered to SCOM (TP11).
probePoints.note: Output of the 175 kΩ/25 kΩ internal calibration attenuator on HR8, buffered by chopper-stabilised op amp U9 running on supplies cut down by VR57 and VR58. The published check is 'the voltage at TP12 divided by 8, ±1%'. Two independent sources agree that this comes to 1.625 V: 13 V ÷ 8 is 1.625, and §2-154 states outright that the resulting output during this calibration step is 1.625 V. Fault 3528 puts the same thing a third way, as a nominal gain of 0.125 that must not be off by more than 7%.

probePoints.label: P701 pins 23A/23C (+PA supply)
probePoints.condition: A18's S201 moved to the low voltage test position, per §5-22 step 3. Power the instrument down before moving that switch.
probePoints.note: The published number applies only in the test mode step 3 sets up, where A18 substitutes its unregulated ±44 SR rails for the ±PA supplies so the main loop can be troubleshot at survivable voltages. In normal operation +PA is +185 V or +365 V depending on the output setting -- see Table 2-13 -- and the manual publishes no tolerance for those. A failure here is A18's, not A16's. Leaving S201 in the test position produces fault 3507 at the next power-up.

probePoints.label: P701 pins 25A/25C (-PA supply)
probePoints.condition: A18's S201 moved to the low voltage test position, per §5-22 step 3. Power the instrument down before moving that switch.
probePoints.note: The negative half of the pair. Printed in the manual as '±60V ±15V' for both rails together, so the magnitude is what is published and the sign is applied here. In normal operation -PA is -185 V or -365 V per Table 2-13. Note that fault 3507 fires precisely on a measured magnitude between 40 V and 80 V, which is this test mode's whole range -- the diagnostic is detecting the switch position, not a supply fault.
